terminal.description: A shell that starts in the shop's top folder. Restart gives you a fresh shell when its settings get in a muddle.

tasks.title: Save your home folder
tasks.description:
Save what `echo $HOME` prints in your terminal into `home.txt` in the top folder.

Check reads `home.txt` and compares its one line with the home folder of your account.
nextSteps: Run `echo $HOME` and read what it prints.
Compare it with what `pwd` prints: they are two different folders.
Run the same `echo` again with `>` and the file's name after it.
hints: A `$` in front of a variable's name makes the shell put in its value.
`echo` prints what comes after it, and `>` saves that into a file. The name is in capitals.
Run `echo $HOME > home.txt` from the top folder.

tasks.title: Hand the shop's name to the label script
tasks.description:
`label.sh` prints the top of a parcel label and takes the shop's name from the variable `SHOP_NAME`. In the terminal, set `SHOP_NAME` to `Ashgrove Press` so that `label.sh` sees it, then save what `label.sh` prints into `label.txt` in the top folder.

Check compares `label.txt` with what `label.sh` prints when it gets that name.
nextSteps: Run `sh label.sh` and read the first line it prints.
Set `SHOP_NAME` in the terminal, and run the script again: the name is still missing.
Hand the variable to the programs you start, and run the script again.
Save what it prints with `>`, and look at `label.txt`.
hints: A variable you set stays in the shell. The lesson's part on what a program sees says how to pass it on.
`export` hands a variable to every program you start after it. Keep the name in quotes: it has a space.
Run `export SHOP_NAME="Ashgrove Press"`, then `sh label.sh > label.txt`.

tasks.title: Put the shop's tools on PATH
tasks.description:
Make `bin/stamp` runnable for you. Then add a line to `shop-settings.sh` that adds the full path of the `bin` folder to `PATH`, keeping every folder already on it, so that `stamp` alone runs from any folder once the file is loaded. Keep every line the file has now.

Check reads the permissions of `bin/stamp`, loads `shop-settings.sh` with `sh` in a copy of the top folder, starting in another folder, and looks for `stamp` and for `ls` through `PATH`.
nextSteps: Run `stamp`, then `bin/stamp`, and read both messages.
Find the full path of `bin` with `pwd`, and add the line to `shop-settings.sh`.
Press Restart, load the file with `. ./shop-settings.sh`, and run `stamp` from inside `bin`.
hints: Two things are missing: the permission to run the file, and the folder on the list the shell searches.
`chmod u+x` gives the owner `x`. The new line exports `PATH` as the full path of `bin`, a colon, then `$PATH`, all in quotes.
Run `chmod u+x bin/stamp`, then add the line `export PATH="<what pwd prints>/bin:$PATH"` to shop-settings.sh, with the real path in place of the part in angle brackets.

tasks.title: Keep the shop's name for next time
tasks.description:
Add a line to `shop-settings.sh` that sets `SHOP_NAME` to `Ashgrove Press` for every program started after the file is loaded. Keep every line the file has now.

Check loads `shop-settings.sh` with `sh` in a copy of the top folder, starting in another folder, then runs `label.sh` and reads the name it prints.
nextSteps: Press Restart, run `sh label.sh`, and see that the name is gone again.
Add the line to the end of `shop-settings.sh`.
Run `sh label.sh` and read the first line.
hints: The line is the one that made the label right in the terminal. In the file, it is read every time the file is loaded.
Set and export the name in one line, with the name in quotes. Add it with the editor or with `>>`.
Add the line `export SHOP_NAME="Ashgrove Press"` to the end of shop-settings.sh.
